record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Polyomino Tilings
record.context_brief: Complexity of recognizing r distinct tilings
record.original_question: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a polyomino and an integer r, decides whether the polyomino has exactly r distinct tilings of the plane?

evidence.quote: Grünbaum and Shephard [22] considered shapes inducing a finite number of tilings r, later called r-morphic shapes [11]
Following the progression in a previous section, in which the existential problem is followed by algorithmic one, how difficult is it to determine how many tilings a polyomino has?
Open Problem 15 Is there a polynomial-time algorithm for determining whether a polyomino has r distinct tilings?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polyomino is a finite, edge-connected union of unit squares in the integer lattice Z^2 (taken up to translation; rotations and reflections may also be allowed as congruences). A tiling of the plane by a polyomino P is a covering of R^2 by interior-disjoint isometric copies of P. Two tilings are considered distinct if they are not equal as labeled coverings (equivalently, one is not obtained from the other by an isometry preserving the tiling). A polyomino is called r-morphic if it admits exactly r distinct tilings of the plane.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm which, given as input a polyomino P (described by its constituent unit squares) and a positive integer r, decides in time polynomial in the size of P and in r whether P has exactly r distinct tilings of the plane?
artifact.status_search_result: Polynomial-time algorithms are known for related decision problems (e.g., whether a polyomino admits an isohedral tiling, or whether translates of a polyomino tile the plane), but no algorithm is known that, given a polyomino and an integer r, decides in polynomial time whether the polyomino has exactly r distinct plane tilings. Counting the number of tilings appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: An algorithm for deciding if a polyomino tiles the plane
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial-time algorithm for deciding whether translates of a polyomino tile the plane.
status_evidence.claim: Related polynomial decisional results exist but do not count tilings.

status_evidence.title: Isohedral Polyomino Tiling of the Plane
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial time algorithm for isohedral tiling existence.
status_evidence.claim: Counting distinct tilings remains a separate, open question.
